_readme: Word-for-word text from the official PDFs. Do not edit the wording: it is canon. Typos in the PDFs are kept on purpose. A paragraph is a list of pieces: a plain string, or an object. {"pin": id} makes the words clickable onto the evidence board. {"redacted": true} is a black bar that never lifts (redacted in the PDF too). {"clearance": stageId} hides the words behind a bar until that stage is cleared. {"strong": true} is bold. {"signature": name} is a signature line (art slot). {"hand": true} is handwriting. {"penNote": {...}} adds a red-pen note beside the words once a stage is cleared; the note's text must be quoted from a canon document. A document with "sealedUntil": stageId can't be opened until that stage is cleared. "timeline" lists dated events from the documents ("source" is the document id). The two code files (OriginalCode.txt, AlteredCode.txt) stay in the project root and are loaded directly by the terminal.

text: A preliminary physical inspection of The Reckoning V: Origins was conducted following the reported operational irregularities. The machine remained identifiable and structurally intact at the time of inspection. No evidence of catastrophic structural failure, major enclosure displacement, or widespread fragmentation was recorded during the visual assessment. The external housing exhibited several minor surface irregularities, including localised scuffing near the lower access panel, superficial abrasions along the right-side casing, and a small area of discolouration adjacent to a ventilation opening. These findings were confined to the exterior surfaces and did not, on visual examination alone, establish damage to any internal assembly.
The following conditions were documented during the inspection:

a. Enclosure surface damage: Fine scratches and shallow abrasions were observed on the outer casing. Their distribution was irregular, and no distinctive pattern was identified that would establish a particular impact direction or mechanism.
b. Access-panel alignment:

text.text: A slight, visually perceptible offset was noted along one edge of the lower access panel.

text: The panel remained attached, and no conclusion regarding interference with internal components could be drawn from its external position alone.

c. Ventilation grille: A small accumulation of dust and fibrous debris was present along portions of the ventilation grille. No verified airflow restriction or associated thermal consequence was established.
d. Surface discolouration:

text.text: Localised darkening was observed near one ventilation aperture.

text: The material's composition and the origin of the discolouration were not determined. The observation cannot independently be classified as evidence of overheating, combustion, or electrical arcing.
e. Fastener condition: Minor cosmetic wear was visible around two externally accessible fastener heads. No verified loss of fastening integrity or corresponding structural instability was recorded.

The physical findings do not independently establish a connection with the electrical irregularities documented in the accompanying report. In particular, the recorded compressor-controller startup and elevated harmonic content remain observations of undetermined significance. No verified physical evidence currently links either observation to the enclosure abrasions, surface discolouration, or panel misalignment.

Similarly, no specific physical defect was identified as the initiating cause of the reported operational event. The available observations are insufficient to determine whether the superficial conditions predated the incident, developed during normal operation, or arose in connection with the event itself.

The inspection documented limited external wear and several minor surface anomalies. Within the scope of the preliminary visual assessment, no major external structural failure was established. The condition of concealed components, internal supports, electrical insulation, and load-bearing assemblies remains unverified and should not be inferred from the exterior findings.

The physical inspection produced a record of superficial enclosure irregularities but did not establish a specific mechanical failure, a causal sequence, or a definitive relationship between the observed surface conditions and the reported electrical anomalies. All findings remain preliminary and are limited to the conditions actually documented during inspection.

rows: From: Department of Electricity, Government of nuxEland
To: Extradigital Exceptions and Unknowns Network

The Department of Electricity hereby furnishes the enclosed electricity consumption records and associated meter readings for Wenoti Arcade, pursuant to the formal request submitted by Agents Nano and Mega of EXUN. These figures have been compiled from the available metering records and are provided to support the ongoing investigation into the reported anomalies.
Records submitted at the request of

text: The following observations were noted during data review but have not been established:

items: HVAC startup coincidence: The facility's compressor controller recorded a startup.
Elevated harmonic content: The readings are compatible with switching electronics operating under changing load conditions.
Minor phase imbalance: A small phase increase was recorded, although no single phase accounts for the total demand excursion.

text: No substantial thermal excursion was observed at the accessible measurement points during the event. The short duration of the peak may limit the extent to which a thermal response would be apparent at these locations. These findings do not exclude localised heating within inaccessible components. No conclusion can be drawn regarding internal semiconductor temperatures without additional instrumentation.
It is uncompromisable that any relevant discrepancies identified in the accompanying data should be referred and forwarded with expedience to the Department for further verification.

log.title: Progress Assesment Log
log.author: Agent Nano
log.concern: A VIDEO GAME CHARACTER HAS ESCAPED INTO THE REAL WORLD
log.question: WHY?

rows.text: OK OK OK... listen, LISTEN. I know this is going to sound really insane and you guys probably think I have gone crazy, but it’s all clocking now.
I’m writing this log at 23:54, October 25th.

The past few days have been full of random tests and experiments on that freaky arcade machine but I think I’ve finally cracked the code. LITERALLY, Let’s go all the way back for a minute. That electricity report energy dossier thing. There was a huge energy spike on the 23rd and that’s what started all of this.
That’s the same night me and Agent Mega met POI-1 at the Reckoning machine, that weird cosplayer. BUT BUT BUT BUT BUT.
When we finally got the game source code on the 24th, the code analysts reverted and told me that one of the character “classes” (coding thing) was completely missing.
That could only mean one thing... The character. Escaped. But the bigger, more worrying question is
If my theory is correct, then A VIDEO GAME CHARACTER HAS ESCAPED INTO THE REAL WORLD!!!! CALL THE MILITARY!!
Immediate concern?? 10/10??? Code red? Blue? Green? All of them?!
